messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: multiple SRV lookup failures observed from services in us-west-2b. Alert group: service-discovery. Initial spike at 2026-03-15T21:22:23Z (thread created). Severity: P2. Symptoms: internal requests to model-routing service returning 502/503 from clients that rely on SRV records; fallback to A-records sometimes succeeds.

pagerduty: Paging oncall (us-west): kevin_h -> please ack. :rotating_light:

kevin_h: acked. I'm looking at the dashboard — spikes in srv_lookup_error_rate on coredns-proxy in us-west-2b. Error signature looks like truncated SRV responses + occasional NXDOMAINs.

maria_g: attaching quick metric snapshot: srv_errors per minute: us-west-2b=480, us-west-2a=6, us-east1=3. Upstream consul health shows leader flaps in us-west-2b for the last 7m.

sanjay_r: can we confirm whether it's the DNS layer (CoreDNS) or the service registry (Consul/etcd) returning inconsistent records? If consul returning different TTLs across replicas we could see TTL regen mismatch and stale cached entries.

emily_z: running live dig from a failing host: ```
; >>HEADER<< flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;_modelgrpc._tcp.redwood.internal. IN SRV
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 23845
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 12
```  — intermittent SERVFAILs. Also saw a few full SRV answers with only 1/3 expected records.

oncall-ml: Observed client-side error rates up ~3x for streaming endpoints in us-west-2 region. Estimated affected tokens: small fraction currently but customer-facing inference endpoints for some low-latency customers are impacted. Not a full outage, but degraded.

kevin_h: immediate mitigation plan: 1) short-circuit SRV usage in router for failsafe routes to fall back to A-records for 5m; 2) restart coredns pods in us-west-2b one-at-a-time; 3) drain & rebalance consul server in us-west-2b if the restart doesn't stabilize. I can take steps 1 & 2 now.

ops-tilt: +1 on incremental approach. Before restarts, capture pcap & tcpdump on node to verify truncated UDP responses vs TCP fallback. Command: `kubectl exec -n infra -c coredns coredns-proxy-xyz -- tcpdump -n -w /tmp/dump.pcap udp port 53`

maria_g: logs from coredns-proxy-0 (tail): ```
2026-03-15T21:23:15Z ERR svc_lookup: consul response truncated for service=\"_modelgrpc._tcp.redwood.internal\" client=10.3.12.45
2026-03-15T21:23:16Z WARN upstream: consul server 10.1.7.11 returned inconsistent TTLs (10s vs 60s) for same service
```

sanjay_r: that TTL variance is suspicious — sounds like a split-brain or leader lag. Querying consul directly from the consul servers.

emily_z: running `dig @10.1.7.11 _modelgrpc._tcp.redwood.internal SRV +short` -> returns 2 records. `dig @10.1.7.12 ...` -> returns 0 records. So inconsistent state across consul servers.

kevin_h: starting mitigation: applying temporary router change to prefer A-record fallback for SRV failures. Patch rolled to canary (router-uswest-2b) with 10% traffic shift. `kubectl apply -f patch-srv-fallback.yaml` (output: configmap/route-modified created).

oncall-ml: canary shows error rate down 45% for affected clients on canary path. Good signal. Hold while we restart coredns pods.

kevin_h: restarting coredns-proxy pods in us-west-2b one at a time: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/coredns-proxy -n infra --field-selector=metadata.name=coredns-proxy-uswest2b` => pod 0 restarted, pod 1 restarted. Monitoring.

maria_g: after restarts: srv_errors in us-west-2b dropped from 480 -> 70 in 6m. Consul leader remains unstable though — looking into raft logs.

sanjay_r: I see raft heartbeat delays: `WARN raft: heartbeat from leader delayed by 3s` on server 10.1.7.12. Suspect noisy disk IO on that host (host is a VM with high I/O ops). Triggered maintenance on that instance.

emily_z: while we patch consul, I'll add a short advisory to support: \"Intermittent SRV lookup failures in us-west-2b affecting small % of inference requests; mitigation applied (SRV->A fallback + coredns restarts).\"

ops-tilt: started migration: evicting consul replica on 10.1.7.12 and forcing a rebuild: `consul operator raft remove-peer` -> drain -> start new peer in us-west-2a.

kevin_h: rolling traffic back from canary to 100% on patched router while we ensure consistency, then we'll remove fallback once consul fully healthy. Current plan: monitor 20m, if errors < 10/min resume normal SRV routing.

oncall-ml: customer impact note: Support triage: two enterprise customers reported degraded streaming responses; CS notified and given mitigation ETA ~30-45m.

maria_g: 21:37 UTC — raft stabilized, Consul leader elected in us-west-2a, consul queries now consistent across replicas. srv_errors down to 8/min.

kevin_h: removing A-fallback from router in 5 minutes and will test traffic. Rolling change now.

emily_z: after removing fallback, monitoring shows errors remaining < 12/min; latency back to baseline for most customers.

kevin_h: handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Handoff to sanjay_r for the next 2 hours for post-incident stabilization and follow-ups (logs, RCA). @sanjay_r you good to take? :handshake:

sanjay_r: taking it. I'll collect raft logs and open an incident ticket for deeper root cause (noisy IO on consul host + inadequate cross-AZ replica placement).

oncall-ml: acknowledged handoff. I'll update the incident page and notify CS to close the customer advisory once we confirm 60m of stability.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-32 (SRV TTL/consul inconsistency in us-west-2b). Severity set to P2. Owners: sanjay_r, emily_z. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0315-32

maria_g: postmortem TODOs captured: - add health check for TTL variance across consul replicas - improve placement policy so majority quorum not in same AZ under noisy IO risk - add automatic SRV->A fallback toggle runbook - investigate UDP truncation thresholds for coredns -> consul queries.

ops-tilt: leaving notes in runbook: `if SRV errors spike only in one AZ: 1) enable SRV->A fallback 2) restart coredns pods 3) check consul raft/IO 4) migrate replica` — add this to ops runbook after RCA.

kevin_h: thanks team. I'll close my page. Good work. :thumbsup:
